content: This argument is a no-op write: `app` is the same row instance read at the top of `onPackageInstalled` (`repo.getAppByPackage(packageName)`), so passing `app.installedVersion` simply rewrites the tag column with the value it already holds. Preserving the tag is the intended "observe zone" behaviour (as documented in `InstalledAppUpdates.kt` and implemented by `SyncInstalledAppsUseCase.syncVersion` via `observeExternalInstall(...) + updateApp(...)`), but expressing it as a write of the row's own value is implicit and fragile: if the row is mutated between the read and this call (e.g. a concurrent install confirmation), this write would silently roll the tag back to the stale value. Prefer an observe-specific repository/DAO path that does not include `installedVersion` in the UPDATE, so the "external observations never touch the tag" invariant is enforced rather than implied.

The numeric-suffix test only accepts pure digits, so a marker followed by a *dotted* numeric version is misclassified as opaque while an equivalent non-dotted one is not:

content:
Two gaps versus the Manga implementation:

1. The overrides are only honoured by the `Primary` variant; `Tonal`, `Outline`, `Text` and `Destructive` ignore `containerColor`/`contentColor` entirely, while `MangaButton` applies them to **every** variant. A call such as `KomiButton(variant = KomiButtonVariant.Outline, containerColor = …)` is a silent no-op under `ClassicPersonality` but is applied under `MangaPersonality`, so behaviour diverges between personalities for the same public API.
2. Only the *enabled* colours are overridden. `ButtonDefaults.buttonColors` leaves `disabledContainerColor`/`disabledContentColor` unset, so they fall back to the theme's accent-derived disabled colours. A disabled button that was pinned to a fixed colour therefore reverts to an accent-tinted colour — which defeats the stated purpose of not following the accent (and differs from Manga, where the fixed colour is kept and only faded by `alpha = 0.45f`).

Consider deriving the disabled colours from the override (e.g. `containerColor.copy(alpha = 0.12f)` / `contentColor.copy(alpha = 0.38f)`) and either honouring the override for all variants or documenting the `Primary`-only restriction in the KDoc of `KomiButton`.

```kotlin
): ButtonColors {

```
Yes. And `ColorScheme.defaultButtonColors` = `ButtonColors(containerColor = primary, contentColor = onPrimary, disabledContainerColor = primary.copy(alpha=DisabledContainerOpacity), disabledContentColor = onPrimary.copy(alpha=DisabledContentOpacity))` — actually I think defaultButtonColors uses `onSurface.copy(alpha = 0.38f)` for disabledContentColor. Either way, theme/accent derived. So the claim is accurate for versions using takeOrElse; in the older direct-assign version, disabledContainerColor would be `Color.Unspecified` → Button resolves... `colors.containerColor(enabled=false)` = disabledContainerColor = Unspecified → nothing drawn (transparent)? In that version, Button has:

```kotlin

```
and ButtonColors disabledContainerColor default = Color.Unspecified → the button would render with unspecified color (effectively transparent). Hmm. Consider a wrapping `FlowRow` for the action group, or let the dialog/button row wrap instead of forcing `SpaceBetween` on one line.

The strip reserved here by `navigationBarsPadding()` is left unpainted: the padding is applied to `SharedTransitionLayout`, so it shrinks the constraints of the `NavHost` below, and the only background in this subtree is `NavHost`'s own `Modifier.background(...)` (line 174), which therefore covers just the inset content area. Before this change `KomiScaffold`'s `Scaffold` filled the whole window with `colors.background`, so the area behind the (transparent, edge-to-edge) navigation bar matched the app theme; now the window background (`Theme.AppCompat.DayNight` → white/#303030) shows through, which does not match personalities such as AMOLED black or the manga paper tones.

Suggestion: paint the container that also receives the insets, e.g. add `Modifier.background(LocalPersonality.current.colors.background)` at the start of this modifier chain (before `.padding(...)`, so the background also draws the padded area), or put the background on the outer `Box` at line 133.

`recordSession` covers the `getUser()` (no token), `primeSession()` and `logout()` paths, but not `notifySessionExpired()`, which also clears the token (`tokenStore.clear()` at line 169). After a 401-driven expiry, `_lastKnownSession` keeps reporting `isLoggedIn = true` together with the old account. The only thing that currently corrects this is `ProfileViewModel` calling `clearLastKnownSession()` when its `isUserLoggedIn()` collector emits `false` — and that collector only exists while the profile screen has been visited, so any other screen (including the new avatar warm-up in `MainViewModel`, which reads `lastKnownSession?.profile?.imageUrl`) can keep seeing a session that no longer exists, and the profile screen can be seeded from it on first frame.

The interface doc states `clearLastKnownSession()` is called "wherever the token is found to be gone"; since this class is the single owner of the token, it should record the signed-out session itself on that path rather than relying on a UI-layer observer. Consider adding `recordSession(isLoggedIn = false, profile = null)` (or `clearLastKnownSession()`) right after the `tokenStore.clear()` call in `notifySessionExpired()`.

This warm-up request sets no `size`, so Coil decodes it at the source's full resolution (GitHub avatars are ~460px) instead of the ~80dp the profile actually draws. Two consequences:

1. `GitHubStoreImage` renders the avatar through `rememberAsyncImagePainter(model = ...)` with a plain URL, so its request size is resolved from the layout constraints (~80dp). Coil keys memory-cache entries per request (`memoryCacheKey` + requested size, see `MarkdownImageTransformer` which deliberately sets `.size(...).memoryCacheKey(...)` for cross-composition reuse). A differently sized warm-up request therefore does not reliably seed the entry the profile looks up, which defeats the stated purpose of the warm-up.
2. Even when it is reused, the memory cache ends up holding a full-size bitmap that is then downscaled for an 80dp view.

Consider requesting the size the avatar is displayed at and pinning a stable `memoryCacheKey` (e.g. `.size(avatarSize).memoryCacheKey(url)`), and having `GitHubStoreImage` use the same `memoryCacheKey` for the avatar so both requests resolve to one entry.

content: Seeding `isUserLoggedIn = true` together with a `null` profile can produce a contradictory first frame. `HeroIdentityCard` branches on `userProfile == null` (rendering `SignedOutContent`, i.e. the "Sign in" CTA), while `library_header`/`library_list`/`account_list` branch on `isUserLoggedIn`. This combination is reachable whenever the process has a token but no cached/stale profile (`primeSession` records exactly that), and it survives as long as `getUser()` takes to resolve — so the very first frame the user sees is a "Sign in" card sitting above the signed-in-only Stars row and the Logout row. Consider deriving the seed consistently (or rendering a loading state in the hero card for `isUserLoggedIn && userProfile == null` instead of the sign-in CTA).

content: `clearLastKnownSession()` here makes this screen's collector the only thing keeping the snapshot honest, but the repository drops the token in other paths without touching the snapshot — notably `notifySessionExpired()`, which calls `tokenStore.clear()` and never calls `recordSession(...)`. If the session expires while this ViewModel does not exist yet, `lastKnownSession` stays `(isLoggedIn = true, profile = <previous account>)`, and the next `ProfileViewModel` seeds its first frame from that stale account before the token flow corrects it. Prefer invalidating the snapshot inside the repository wherever the token is cleared, so the seed can never be stale regardless of which screen happens to be alive.

content: `primeSession()` trusts the `profile:me` cache entry without any check that it belongs to the token currently in the store, and that entry is only ever cleared by `logout()` — the 401 path in `notifySessionExpired()` clears the token but leaves the cached profile behind (TTL 6h). If a session expires and a different GitHub account signs in afterwards on the same device, this records (and `ProfileViewModel` renders on its first frame, plus `MainViewModel` warms) the *previous* account's profile/avatar. Since `getUser()`'s cache-hit path has the same blind spot, keying the entry by the owning token/account (e.g. `"profile:me:$accessToken"`) or at least invalidating the entry when no token is present the way `getUser()` does (see below) would bound the risk.
